lines.trans: Yes, this black caviar is indeed very tasty.
How much money did you prepare for five kilograms?
Name the exact price for all these goods.
That will be exactly two hundred thousand rubles right now.
Timur, leave the caviar, and I will pay later.
No money — no delicious caviar.
I bet all the money on your advice!
You lost on your favorite fast horses.
You yourself swore by their victory!
Let your horses bring caviar to you now.
Why are you taking this merchandise back?
By the way, return three hundred rubles for this spoon!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: moving or capable of moving at high speed

examples.text: Они сказали, что устанавливают быстрый интернет.
examples.trans: They said that they were installing fast internet.

examples.text: Большое спасибо за вашу быструю помощь!
examples.trans: Thank you very much for your quick help!

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

вернуть.gloss: to give back, to get back

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give back', forming an aspectual pair with 'возвращать'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to get back') (money you spent) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tasty, delicious').

examples.trans: The bread rings are very tasty.

examples.text: Марина Сергеевна, присядьте. Попробуйте чай с сушками, очень вкусные.
examples.trans: Marina Sergeyevna, have a seat. Try the tea with bread rings, they're very tasty.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian numeral ('two hundred') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.text: Двести десять на сто тридцать девять!
examples.trans: Two hundred and ten over one hundred and thirty-nine!

examples.text: С тебя ровно двести тысяч рублей прямо сейчас.
examples.trans: That will be exactly two hundred thousand rubles right now.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Настроение у меня действительно очень хорошее.
examples.trans: My mood really is very good.
This is indeed an important question.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('behind') (+ instrumental) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'what for'.

examples.trans: Oh, Samson. What have you come for?

meanings.note: красная икра = red (salmon) caviar, чёрная икра = black caviar

examples.text: Мама говорила, что у меня на икру аллергия.
examples.trans: Mum said I'm allergic to caviar.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'kilogram', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Give me two kilograms of apples, please.

examples.text: Говорят, собака нашла запах плохой травы! Тут пять килограммов сгорело!
examples.trans: They say the dog found the smell of bad herbs! Five kilograms burned here!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to swear', forming an aspectual pair with 'поклясться'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Клянусь честью повара, я не брал твой японский нож!
examples.trans: I swear on my honor as a cook, I did not take your Japanese knife!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'horse; knight (in chess)' in everyday Russian.
Secondary conversational sense ('knight (chess piece)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is a knight, and this is a queen.

examples.text: Ты проиграл на своих любимых быстрых конях.
examples.trans: You lost on your favorite fast horses.

meanings.en: by the way, speaking of which
meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'by the way'.
Secondary conversational sense ('handy, well-timed') (это очень кстати) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, by the way, I almost forgot.

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: чайная ложка = teaspoon, столовая ложка = tablespoon

examples.trans: He eats soup with a spoon.
And take his eye out with a spoon.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('favourite, beloved').
Secondary conversational sense ('beloved, darling') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой!
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake!

examples.text: А ты готовишь мой любимый торт со сгущёнкой! До вечера, Марина.
examples.trans: And you make my favourite condensed milk cake! See you tonight, Marina.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: кого + instrumental: назвать меня плохим словом
Secondary conversational sense ('to name') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You called me a bad word.
What will you name your son?

examples.text: Ты назвал меня плохим словом. Меня, начальника!
examples.trans: You called me a bad word. Me, your boss!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('no ... at all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: I have no money at all.

examples.text: Да нет у тебя никаких денег.
examples.trans: But you don't have any money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'ратно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

examples.text: Вот это дело! Потом обратно бесплатно отвезу.
examples.trans: Now we're talking! Afterwards I'll drive you back for free.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('they') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to leave', forming an aspectual pair with 'оставлять'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('to keep, to save') (оставь мне кусок = save me a piece) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I won't leave him on his own.

examples.text: Вика, ну он одинокий. Я же не оставлю его одного.
examples.trans: Vika, come on, he's all alone. I can't just leave him on his own.

meanings.en: to give away, to hand over
meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'дать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to give', forming an aspectual pair with 'отдавать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to give back') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: He will hand over the money.

examples.text: Потом надо отдать москвичам твои деньги из подвала.
examples.trans: Then I have to give your money from the basement to the Moscow people.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'very'.
Secondary conversational sense ('very much') (with verbs: очень люблю) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'along' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('along, around') (+ dative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('by (phone)') ('по телефону') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'victory', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Люди в городе аплодируют вашей победе!
examples.trans: People in the town are applauding your victory!

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'later'.

examples.trans: Go on, come by later! Later!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'ставить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to install') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Put your foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'носить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bring', paired with 'принести'.

examples.text: Я приношу бутылку шампанского и свечи.
examples.trans: I'll bring a bottle of champagne and candles.

examples.text: И не надо больше никаких документов сюда приносить!
examples.trans: And don't bring any more documents in here!

meanings.note: money, a game, a bet, or an election

examples.trans: I lost it on the stock exchange.

examples.text: Денег нет, Самсон. Я их на бирже проиграл.
examples.trans: There is no money, Samson. I lost it on the stock exchange.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('five') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.text: Мы же только начинаем. Через месяц будет пять тысяч.
examples.trans: But we're only just starting. In a month there'll be five thousand.

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Secondary conversational sense ('evenly, smoothly') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'rouble', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.
examples.trans: Our task is to take a billion roubles from the bribe-takers.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'how much'.
Secondary conversational sense ('what a lot of!') (in exclamations) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
общественный совет = public council
Secondary conversational sense ('piece of advice') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Это правильно. Я приглашаю вас в общественный совет.
examples.trans: That's right. I'm inviting you onto the public council.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'now'.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'goods, merchandise' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тимур, не наглей и отдавай товар!
examples.trans: Timur, don't get cheeky and hand over the goods!

examples.text: Сейчас я сразу оценю твой дорогой товар.
examples.trans: Now I will immediately evaluate your expensive goods.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('exact, precise').

examples.trans: Wait, is this information accurate at all?

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('three hundred') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.text: А для него это как триста!
examples.trans: And for him it's like three hundred!
The ticket costs three hundred roubles.

examples.text: Триста пятьдесят миллионов рублей по смете!
examples.trans: Three hundred and fifty million rubles per estimate!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'бирать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to clean up, to tidy', paired with 'убрать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to put away') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'price, cost' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ого, двадцать тысяч рублей? Ничего себе цена!
examples.trans: Wow, twenty thousand rubles? What a price!

examples.text: Тогда цена выросла до семисот евро!
examples.trans: Then the price has risen to seven hundred euros!

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('black').

examples.trans: Listen, look in the black cabinet.

examples.text: На нём был строгий чёрный костюм.
examples.trans: He was wearing a formal black suit.

examples.text: Как не нашла? Послушай, в чёрном шкафу посмотри. Там справа от двери!
examples.trans: What do you mean you didn't find it? Listen, look in the black cabinet. There to the right of the door!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
